rows.title: doesn't apply right fix comment in jsx/tsx context
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the investigation in this thread. This remains the canonical request for context-aware disable comments: current main still chooses comment syntax from the document language ID, so it cannot distinguish JSX markup from ordinary JavaScript or TypeScript within the same file. The most promising editor-independent direction remains using the parser from ESLint's resolved configuration to inspect the ESTree at the diagnostic location and emit JSX-safe `{/* ... */}` syntax only when needed.

rows.title: More visibility for workingDirectories setting
jsonschema: source.fixAll.eslint does not seem to exist
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. The extension already provides and handles `source.fixAll.eslint`, but completion for `editor.codeActionsOnSave` is owned by VS Code's settings schema. The generic contribution-point proposal at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/82718 was later closed as out of scope, while the extension-side schema augmentation suggested here is not present in the current manifest. This remains a useful ESLint-specific discoverability request, with the implementation depending on what augmentation VS Code's settings schema supports.

rows.title: Provide a "basics" setup documentation for VSCode, ESLint & autoformatting
rows.labels: feature-request, help wanted, good first issue
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request and the contribution. This is now covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2164: the README includes ESLint installation and config-generation guidance, a global `editor.codeActionsOnSave` example for automatic ESLint fixes, and a workspace `eslint.validate` example. The documentation shipped in the 3.0.33 pre-release and is also included in stable 3.0.34, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.

rows.title: eslint.nodePath only works with absolute paths in multi module vscode workspaces
File exists, but `ENOENT: no such file or directory...` reported.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the detailed follow-up. This failure path was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/d8214448aa1ba338c84184239bfee66cea24fbaa: errors from `fs.realpathSync.native` are now caught and the server falls back to the original file path, so an ENOENT from realpath no longer silently prevents validation. The fix first shipped in the 2.4.1 pre-release and is also included in stable 2.4.2 and later. The fix shipped in release/2.4.2.

rows.title: Reporting errors from node_module and no way to suppress/disable (also ignores .eslintignore)`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The command-line test confirms that ESLint itself attempts to load the dependency's legacy `eslintConfig` before it determines that the file is ignored. The extension delegates both configuration and ignore resolution to the workspace's ESLint library, and `eslint.onIgnoredFiles` only controls warnings after ESLint has successfully classified a file as ignored. ESLint tracked and confirmed this behavior in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/14686, but decided not to change the frozen legacy eslintrc implementation.

[Feature Request] Add long paths support
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is already being tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1229, including reports where paths around or above the Windows 256-character boundary are not linted by the extension even though the ESLint CLI succeeds. Your additional evidence is useful: lint-staged can fix the same file, while fix-on-save cannot see it until the path is shortened. Let's consolidate the long-path investigation in that issue.

rows.title: Customize error/warning message in VSCode
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed context. This gap is still present on current main: the server flattens newlines in configuration-error messages before displaying them, and custom errors that do not match one of the recognized configuration-error shapes are logged without opening the same notification. There also isn't an `eslint.*` setting that covers this presentation. Keeping this as a feature request to separate full output-channel detail from a concise, readable notification and to decide how multiline messages and package-manager paths should be handled.

rows.title: Use from CLI?
Support basic formatting in hint popup for `no-restricted-*`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request and examples. VS Code's diagnostic API currently exposes the message as a plain string, so the extension cannot preserve links or inline-code formatting here. The broader platform capability is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/54272, which covers Markdown or other formatted diagnostic content. I'll consolidate this request there.

rows.title: Prefer to use node from environment
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for continuing to document the impact. This remains a valid feature request, but selecting an environment-provided executable is security-sensitive. The direction under consideration is therefore a runtime-selection setting that can prefer `node` in trusted workspaces and fall back to the runtime shipped with VS Code when it cannot be resolved, while retaining the safe bundled behavior for untrusted workspaces. The related work in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/1977 may help with workspace-aware resolution, but it does not by itself implement the default-selection behavior requested here.

rows.title: Feature Request: enable the "eslint.format.enable" setting by default.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. “Formatting pipelines” here refers to VS Code's formatter infrastructure, not the Azure Pipelines extension. Multiple extensions can provide formatting, and users select the provider they want—often per language—with `editor.defaultFormatter`. Enabling ESLint's formatter unconditionally would make it participate for users who intentionally use TypeScript, Prettier, or another formatter, and changing the existing default would break those configurations. For that reason, `eslint.format.enable` is intentionally opt-in; users who want ESLint formatting can enable it and select `dbaeumer.vscode-eslint` as their default formatter for the relevant languages.

rows.title: A change to eslint.debug requires VSCode restart if the ESLint server was already running
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and confirmations. Current `main` still explains this behavior: the client computes the server launch options, including the `DEBUG` environment variable from `eslint.debug`, only when the `LanguageClient` is created. The normal restart command calls `client.restart()` on that existing client, so it reuses the stale launch options. Restarting the server should honor the current setting; keeping this open as a bug.

Support for `typescript-eslint` v8's parser `projectService`
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction and follow-up reports. This is a specific instance of the broader cross-file state invalidation problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1774, which covers typescript-eslint project state as well as other parsers and plugins with inter-file dependencies.

The reload added in typescript-eslint 8.3.0 mitigates the initial “file was not found” case, but the later pnpm/Vue and new-folder reports here show why it is not a complete watcher or invalidation solution. Those details are useful evidence for the broader issue, so they should be carried forward there while the extension-side revalidation and parser API are designed together.

Issues with PNPM module resolution
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for continuing to narrow this down. The repository at https://github.com/angryermine/vscode-eslint-pnpm now appears sufficient to exercise the pnpm-specific path, but a Codespace must first have its automatically npm-installed `node_modules` removed and then be installed exclusively with `pnpm install`; https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1986#issuecomment-3660905000 confirms that this changes the result. The remaining question is whether the extension can safely reproduce the resolution environment created by `pnpm eslint`, or whether pnpm 10 projects using legacy shareable configs must explicitly restore ESLint hoisting with `public-hoist-pattern[]=*eslint*`.

rows.title: respect estlint-suppressions.json
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and discussion. Bulk-suppression support landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/9d33f02b2ddaadc55f7f30dfd2338ccca12dc798 and is now available in stable version 3.0.34. With ESLint 10.1 or newer, `eslint.bulkSuppression.enable` enables suppression processing; `eslint.bulkSuppression.severity` controls how suppressed violations appear, and `eslint.bulkSuppression.location` can select a non-default suppression file. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.

rows.title: Measure rule performance through VSCode ESLint
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. `eslint.options` is passed to the workspace ESLint API, so `"stats": true` can already enable statistics on ESLint versions that support it. The missing part is that the server currently consumes the lint messages but does not capture or log the returned `stats` data. There is no ESLint-executable override for a wrapper—the extension loads ESLint as a library, while `eslint.runtime` controls the Node runtime. A suitable implementation would handle the returned stats in the server and write a structured summary to the existing ESLint output channel.

Request: add quick-fix action for adding same-line disables, i.e. `// eslint-disable-line`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. `eslint.codeAction.disableRuleComment.location` does support choosing `"sameLine"` globally, which is a useful workaround. The remaining request here is different: expose both same-line and separate-line quick fixes for each diagnostic so the choice can be made contextually without changing the setting. That is also distinct from the automatic JSX/TSX detection tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1074, so this should remain open as a feature request.

rows.title: css support
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. CSS should be autodetected when using flat config and a current ESLint version, so a minimal GitHub repository that can be cloned and demonstrates the difference from the CLI is needed to investigate this. Please also include the extension and workspace ESLint versions and the contents of the `ESLint` output channel after opening an affected CSS file.

rows.title: /* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */  will disappear when save
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for providing the sample project. Its TypeScript preset enables `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` and disables the core `no-unused-vars` rule, so `/* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */` does not suppress the diagnostic. ESLint consequently reports that directive as unused, and fix-on-save removes it. Please use `/* eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars */` instead; using the extension's disable-rule quick fix will insert the active rule ID automatically.

rows.title: When ESLint is set to automatically fix on save in VsCode, it will remove the first letter
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional settings. A minimal GitHub repository that can be cloned is still needed to determine which save participant produces this edit. Please include the affected source and ESLint configuration, the ESLint extension, VS Code, and workspace ESLint versions, and the contents of the `ESLint` output channel after reproducing it. It would also help to confirm whether the first character is still removed when `editor.codeActionsOnSave` contains only `"source.fixAll.eslint": "explicit"`, with the TSLint, Stylelint, Prettier, and general `source.fixAll` entries disabled.

rows.title: docs: Document for `eslint.lintTask.command` is missing
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for catching this and for opening https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2126. That PR adds the missing `eslint.lintTask.command` entry, so this issue should remain open while the documentation change is reviewed.

rows.title: ESLint plugin breaks when using `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The updated task-specific steps explain why this differs from normal per-file linting: `lint whole folder` shells out to ESLint and VS Code builds Problems entries by parsing its stdout with `$eslint-stylish`, while open-file validation uses the ESLint language server directly. The React Hooks rules emit multiline messages with source excerpts, and the core matcher expects each diagnostic and rule ID on one physical line. The broader matcher limitation is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/9635, so I propose consolidating this there. The useful case to carry over is ESLint 9.39.3 with eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.0.1 and `yarn eslint .`, where the task output contains all diagnostics but the Problems view retains only a subset.

rows.title: Eslint client couldn't create connection to server after installing new VS Code version
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. I haven't been able to reproduce this server-start failure with current versions, and there hasn't been a confirmation that it still occurs, so I'm closing this as not reproducible. If it happens again, please open a new issue with the current ESLint extension and VS Code versions, the latest `ESLint` output-channel content, and whether `eslint.runtime` or `eslint.execArgv` is configured.

rows.title: ESLint version 10.0.3 only supports flat configs. Setting is ignored
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2172: the extension no longer forwards the deprecated `eslint.experimental.useFlatConfig` default when the setting was not explicitly enabled, so ESLint 10 no longer produces this spurious notice. The fix first shipped in pre-release 3.0.25 and is included in stable 3.0.34. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.

rows.title: Extension causes high cpu load
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you attach the CPU profile referenced in the original report? The link points to a temporary file on your local machine, so its contents are not available here. If that profile is no longer available, please capture a new one on the current extension version and include the `ESLint` output-channel contents and, if possible, a minimal GitHub repository that reproduces the high CPU usage.

rows.title: Disable rule quick fixes insert JS-style comments into Markdown files
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and contribution. The current server path confirms the problem: Markdown falls back to JavaScript line and block comments in `languageDefaults.ts`, and the disable-rule actions insert those values unchanged. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2225 is the active fix, so this issue should remain open while that PR is reviewed.
